tldr: The book's most acute risk eased, but did not resolve: Friday's silver/gold-miner rally (SLV +6.20%, GDX +7.16%) moved the levered-silver loan's stressed margin-call distance from -6.8% to -2.1% and leverage down to 2.28x (still over the signed 1.4x ceiling) -- real relief, but the position still fails the 2-day -20%/2-week -35% survivability stress test, so reducing the loan or adding collateral still outranks reading this as resolved.

This is a weekend catch-up run: Thu 26 Nov was US Thanksgiving (markets shut) and Fri 27 Nov's half-day session reversed hard off Wednesday's hot-data air pocket -- S&P +1.60%, Nasdaq +2.31%, VIX -11.16% to 23.81. Asian markets (HK/SG/JP/KR) are closed until Monday.

Two distinct catalysts landed together Friday: China's State Council/Central Huijin stabilization pledge triggered a record +17.6% one-day CSI chip-index rally (SMIC +16.39%, directly in the HK-tech sleeve, alongside Tencent +3.23%/Xiaomi +4.51%), while gold/silver/miners staged a technical short-covering bounce off a 15-month oversold low -- both rode the same risk-on wave despite the Fed staying hawkish (the 10Y and DXY both ROSE the same day, ruling out a rates/dollar-driven reversal).

Hot core PCE (+3.3% y/y), Q3 GDP (revised up to +4.3%) and jobless claims (189K) keep the Fed firmly in a hiking cycle -- prediction markets price ~90-97% odds of another 25bp hike at the Dec 8-9 FOMC, with Waller floating a jumbo 50bp move. Model regime nudged from modest-UW to Neutral on equities and to modest-OW on commodities, reflecting the bounce without calling it a reversal.

Sentiment improved but stayed fearful: CNN-methodology Fear & Greed rose to 25/Fear (from 19) as Friday's breadth fed through, but crypto sentiment barely moved (12/Extreme Fear) and Bitcoin notably did NOT join the rally, holding near $59,800-60,500 -- a narrower risk appetite than headline equity/metals gains suggest.

Smart-money watch: MP Materials' three-officer insider buying cluster (Nov 10-17) remains unanswered by any newer Form 4; BlackRock's DBS stake crossed back below the 5% substantial-shareholder threshold on a 192,000-share sale; Singtel defended its stock with a S$40.7M buyback at an average S$4.07/share the week of Nov 13-19.

Model: macro regime recalibrated for Friday's broad bounce (riskOnProb 0.32 to 0.38; equity stance modest-UW to Neutral; commodities Neutral to modest-OW) without calling it a confirmed reversal. SPY/QQQ/IWM, GLD/SLV, BTC-USD and XLE/USO calls got full driver and probability refreshes for the Friday session; all 40 universe tickers plus the 9-name rare-earth basket remain present.

Market: Fear&Greed advanced to 25/Fear (crypto 12/Extreme Fear, little changed); breadth refreshed to Friday's close (NYSE advancers led decliners ~3.25:1, but the new-low list stayed dominated by mega-cap AI names); flows widget now carries the week-ended-25-Nov edition, flagging a genuine US/EM direction disagreement between Lipper/Reuters and EPFR/Citi for the same week.

Flows-investors: Japan's week-ended-20-Nov report FINALLY published after a 14-day stale gap and several mis-dated-article traps in prior runs; Korea added Friday's first trillion-won foreign net buy since Sep 7; Hong Kong Southbound reversed to net buy (+HK$4.59bn) after Wednesday's 7-month-largest outflow; China added a genuine policy change (minimum margin requirement cut 100% to 80%, effective Nov 30) alongside the daily margin print; Singapore and the US were both genuinely refreshed or honestly carried forward where no newer edition exists yet.

News: 12 items, 9 of 12 dated Nov 26-27, leading with the China stabilization/chip rally and the silver short-covering bounce, plus two genuinely new weekend-adjacent items (Houthi/Ras Tanura oil spike, Arthur Hayes' Fed-blackout crypto warning).

regime.label: Hawkish-Fed, overheating economy -- equity/metals bounce is technical (oversold short-covering + China stimulus), not a risk-appetite or rate-cut regime change
regime.oneLiner: A genuinely broad Friday rally (NYSE advancers ~3.25:1) landed on top of an unresolved hawkish-Fed backdrop -- the 10Y and dollar both rose the same day the metals complex exploded higher, which argues for a technical bounce riding China-stimulus-driven risk appetite rather than a durable regime change.

topNews.headline: China's State Council 'national team'/Central Huijin pledge triggers record 17.6% one-day chip-stock rally; SMIC +16.4%, Hua Hong +20.7%
topNews.actionable: The clearest bullish catalyst for the HK-tech sleeve in weeks -- a genuine policy-driven rally in the chip names specifically -- but confirm it holds through Monday's full session rather than chasing a single holiday-thinned Friday print.

topNews.headline: Silver rockets ~6.9% to $44.44, gold +2% as oversold short-covering bounce follows 15-month low -- analysts warn it is not yet a trend reversal
topNews.actionable: The levered silver position got welcome relief, but because the move is diagnosed as short-covering into a still-hawkish Fed, this reads as a window to de-risk into strength rather than confirmation the squeeze risk has passed.

topNews.headline: Hot Core PCE, upward-revised Q3 GDP and low jobless claims push December 9 Fed hike odds to 94-97%
topNews.actionable: Friday's metals bounce happened despite, not because of, the rates outlook -- near-certain odds of another hike on Dec 9 keep the real-rate headwind for the silver/gold sleeve fully intact.

topNews.headline: Crypto stuck in 'Extreme Fear' (11-12/100) as BTC holds near $60k, didn't join Friday's risk-on rally; Hayes warns of weekend selloff risk as Fed blackout begins
topNews.actionable: Crypto's failure to participate in Friday's broad risk-on move is a useful cross-check against treating the bounce as a broad-based regime change -- not a direct holding, but a sentiment-breadth signal worth tracking.

signals: SHY (front-end Treasuries) remains the model's clearest directional call (pUp3m 0.60, confidence 0.55) -- consider watching as a cash-pile complement while the Dec 9 hike stays priced in; most of the rest of the universe sits closer to coin-flip given the mixed bounce/hawkish-Fed crosscurrent.

The silver/gold-miner complex (HL, GDX, SILJ, SLVP) screens as the strongest multi-source consensus this run -- institutional 13Fs, retail sentiment and Friday's price action all point the same way -- but it's explicitly flagged as short-covering, not fresh demand; worth watching whether the move survives past the Dec 9 FOMC.

MP Materials' three-officer insider buying cluster (Nov 10-17, no newer Form 4 since) remains one of the stronger conviction signals on file; Lynas's NdPr pricing (+88% y/y) is a genuine, independent tailwind for the same ex-China rare-earth basket.

NVDA stays the most contested name on the book's periphery: Congress and retail keep buying (Rand Paul, Cleo Fields, #1 WSB ticker) while Druckenmiller, Soros, Tudor Jones, Caxton and Schonfeld all cut NVDA stakes 19-99% in Q3 13Fs -- worth watching as a sentiment-divergence flag, not a consensus read.
watch: Dec 8-9 FOMC: priced ~90-97% for a 25bp hike, with Waller floating a jumbo 50bp move and Williams not ruling out consecutive hikes -- the single biggest catalyst for both the silver-margin situation and the broader regime.

OPEC+ meets Sun 30 Nov on Q1 2027 quotas, with Iraq and Kazakhstan disputing their new capacity ratings -- a contentious or delayed outcome would add an oil-driven inflation impulse on top of the already-hawkish Fed.

China's gallium/germanium/antimony export-curb truce now runs only to 27 Jan 2027 (a 61-day extension, not the prior year-long reprieve) -- a recurring binary catalyst for the MP/Lynas/UUUU watchlist.
Monday 1 Dec: the first full session (and the first for HK/SG/JP/KR since Friday) to test whether the China-chip and silver/gold bounces hold past a holiday-thinned print.
